text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 29th in history:
1613 - The original Globe Theatre in London burned down during the first performance of Shakespeare's Henry VIII.
1798 - Italian poet Conte Giacomo Leopardi born.
1858 - George Washington Goethals, U.S. engineer who built the Panama Canal and was first governor of the canal zone, born.
1855 - The Daily Telegraph was first published in London.
1861 - William James Mayo, U.S. co-founder of the Mayo Clinic and one of the Mayo family of distinguished surgeons, born.
1868 - The British news agency the Press Association was founded.
1871 - Luisa Tetrazzini, Italian operatic singer and one of the most famous sopranos of her time, born.
1880 - The Pacific island of Otaheite, now better known as Tahiti, was formally annexed by France, having been a French protectorate since 1842.
1886 - Robert Schuman, French statesman and prime minister who pioneered the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC), born.
1900 - Antoine Marie Roger de Saint-Exupery, French aviator and author of "Flight to Arras" and "The Little Prince", born.
1901 - Nelson Eddy, U.S. opera singer and actor who with Jeanette MacDonald made several filmed operettas born.
1910 - Frank Loesser, U.S. composer and lyricist of Broadway hit "Guys and Dolls", born.

1911 - Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands, husband of Queen Juliana and a founder of the World Wildlife Fund, born. His reputation was badly damaged by his involvement in the Lockheed bribery scandal in 1976.
1914 - Rafael Kubelik, Czech conductor and composer of operas, symphonies and concertos, born.
1916 - Irish nationalist Sir Roger Casement was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death for conspiracy with Germany.
1921 - Lady Randolph Churchill (Jennie Jerome), U.S.-born mother of Winston Churchill, died.
1941 - Ignace Jan Paderewski, Polish concert pianist, statesman and prime minister, died in Switzerland.
1943 - Germany began to withdraw its U-Boats from the North Atlantic in anticipation of the Allied invasion of Europe; U.S. forces landed at Nassau Bay, near Salamaua, New Guinea.
1966 - In the Vietnam War, U.S. planes bombed Hanoi and Haiphong for the first time.
1967 - Jayne Mansfield (Vera Jayne Palmer), U.S. film actress, was decapitated in a car crash near New Orleans.
1972 - The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the death penalty was contrary to the constitution.
1974 - Isabel Peron was sworn in as president of Argentina, taking over from her husband Juan Peron who became ill.
1978 - Vietnam became the 10th member of COMECON.
1980 - Vigdis Finnbogadotir was elected Iceland's president, Europe's first democratically elected woman Head of State.
1981 - Hu Yaobang succeeded Hua Guofeng as Chinese Communist Party chairman.
1982 - Pierre Alexandre Balmain, French fashion designer, died.
1990 - Lithuania suspended its declaration of independence for 100 days, pending sovereignty talks with Moscow.
1992 - Algerian head of state Mohamed Boudiaf was assassinated as he opened a cultural centre in the eastern Algerian town of Annaba.
1994 - Japan's parliament chose Socialist Tomiichi Murayama as prime minister at the head of a three-party alliance dominated by conservatives.
1995 - A department store in Seoul collapsed killing 502 people in South Korea's worst peacetime disaster.
1995 - Lana Turner, the blonde bombshell who was discovered at a Hollywood soda fountain and rose to become one of America's most glamorous movie stars, died. She was 75.
1996 - The Bosnian Serb ruling Democratic Party re-elected Radovan Karadzic as leader.
